clue.text: Uncivilised lot showing passion towards male at hen party?

blocks.note: heat is strong feeling, as in the heat of the moment
a hen do is the British name for a bride's pre-wedding party
M is the standard abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A rowdy crowd of women at a hen party leering at the male stripper.
explanation.walkthrough: The passion comes first, then the hen do with the male tacked on at its end: HEAT + HEN DO + M gives HEATHENDOM. A hen do is the British name for a hen party.
explanation.definitionFit: Heathendom is the collective world of heathens, people regarded as unenlightened and uncivilised.

clue.text: Queen’s flag raised by a north African

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising something turns it upside down so it reads from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword queen
to flag is to tire or weaken
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A royal standard is hoisted by someone from North Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' looks like a banner, but here it is the verb meaning to tire. 'North African' reads as one phrase, yet north belongs to the wordplay and African alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: An Eritrean comes from Eritrea, a country on the Red Sea coast in the north-east of Africa.

clue.text: Drink regularly obtained from the bar

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at even intervals, every other one, from the words that follow

blocks.note: first, third and fifth letters of these words

explanation.surface: Someone orders a drink across the counter of a pub as usual.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea is a hot drink brewed from dried leaves, the British staple beverage.

clue.text: Woman turned green before end of journey

indicators.note: something turned round faces the other way, so it is read backwards
the end of a word is its last letter, which is all that is kept

blocks.note: lime is a shade of green
the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: A woman went pale and queasy just before her trip was over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned green' suggests seasickness, but it is a colour written backwards; 'before' puts it ahead of the last letter of journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Emily is a woman's first name, and crosswords often clue a given name with a general word like woman.

clue.text: One will give order for tandoori shortly

indicators.note: made short, the word loses its final letter
to give order to something is to arrange it differently, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the Indian clay-oven dish, taken as written before it is cut

explanation.surface: A diner in an Indian restaurant who will order the tandoori soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give order' reads as placing a restaurant order; 'order' is the anagram signal and 'One will give' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A donator is a person who gives something, typically money to a cause, so the giver of the definition.

clue.text: A feature film about factory worker

indicators.note: something placed about another goes round it, enclosing it

blocks.note: taken as written
the chin is a facial feature
a film or thin layer, as of mist on glass

explanation.surface: A full-length movie made about someone who works in a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feature film' is one phrase in the surface, but it splits into two separate words, each giving its own piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A machinist operates machines, as in a factory or a garment workshop.

clue.text: Animal noise, sound of an equine

indicators.note: the sound of a word is how it is spoken, not how it is spelt

blocks.note: a mule is an equine, the offspring of a donkey and a horse

explanation.surface: A list of farmyard sounds, ending with the noise a horse-like creature makes.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue seems to want a neigh or bray; instead the equine is a mule, whose name is spoken just like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To mewl is to cry feebly or whimper, a sound made by kittens and other small animals.

clue.text: Pantomime fairy and old villainous character standing on sides of stage

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing up means reading from the bottom upwards
the sides of a word are its outermost letters, first and last

blocks.note: Moth is one of Titania's fairies in A Midsummer Night's Dream
O is the abbreviation for old
the ogre is a stock villain of fairy tales
the first and last letters of this word

explanation.surface: A pantomime fairy and the baddie stand together at the edges of the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pantomime fairy' reads as one character, but the definition is just the first word. 'Standing' turns old ogre upside down, and in a down clue 'on' puts it above the stage's sides.
explanation.definitionFit: Mother Goose is a traditional British Christmas pantomime, a family stage show built on a fairy tale.

clue.text: German fellow aboard extremely wobbly rowing boat

indicators.note: someone aboard a vessel is inside it, so one piece goes within another
the extremes of a word are its two end letters

blocks.note: first and last letters of this word
Herr is the German for Mr, a title for a man

explanation.surface: A German man climbs into a very unsteady little rowing boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A wherry is a light rowing boat, historically used to carry passengers on rivers.

clue.text: Following one vehicle round and about becomes an obsession

indicators.note: turned round, the words face the other way and are read backwards

blocks.note: f. is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
I is the Roman numeral one
a taxi is a hired vehicle
on means about, as in a talk on birds

explanation.surface: Chasing a single car round and round turns into a fixation.
explanation.walkthrough: One and the vehicle go backwards together; the 'and' then adds the word for about at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixation is an obsessive attachment or preoccupation with something.

clue.text: Sheffield craftsman maybe retiring about fifty, along with other workers

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so everything that follows is read backwards

blocks.note: re is Latin for about, concerning
L is the Roman numeral fifty
the TUC, Trades Union Congress, is Britain's federation of trade unions

explanation.surface: A Sheffield craftsman retires at about fifty, along with his workmates.
explanation.walkthrough: Retiring looks like stopping work; it reverses RE, L and TUC together. Sheffield is the English city famous for knives and cutlery, hence the 'maybe'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutler makes or sells knives and cutlery, the trade Sheffield is famous for, so a Sheffield craftsman is an example.

clue.text: Shout, squashing a twelve-inch fly?

indicators.note: to squash something is to press it in, so one piece is squeezed inside another

blocks.note: to cry out is to shout
taken as written
twelve inches make a foot, abbreviated ft

explanation.surface: Someone yells while swatting a giant twelve-inch fly.
explanation.walkthrough: The fly looks like an insect to be squashed; here it is the British adjective meaning sharp or cunning.
explanation.definitionFit: Fly is British slang for knowing and sly, a close synonym of crafty.

clue.text: On expedition RAF finally lands here?

definitions.text: On expedition RAF finally lands here

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it
in a down clue, one piece sitting on another is placed above it

blocks.note: last letter of the air force's initials
to light is to land or alight, as a bird lights on a branch
a trip is a journey or excursion

explanation.surface: On an overseas mission, the air force's plane finally touches down here.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes the answer, a place where planes land. In a down clue 'On' stacks the first pieces above the last. The RAF is Britain's Royal Air Force.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight strip is a cleared runway where aircraft take off and land, often a temporary one in the field.

clue.text: Such as soap to test on cotton fabric

indicators.note: one piece placed on another follows it in an across answer

blocks.note: toile is a fine linen or cotton cloth
to try something is to test it

explanation.surface: A product such as soap is tested on cotton cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A toiletry is an item used in washing and grooming, and soap is a typical example.

clue.text: Fashion designer’s work is compulsive

blocks.note: first meaning, read cryptically: shaping habits, which are garments such as a monk's robe
second meaning: tending to create addiction

explanation.surface: A designer's clothes are so desirable that buying them becomes an addiction.
explanation.walkthrough: A habit is a garment as well as a routine, so making habits is literally a dressmaker's job.
explanation.definitionFit: Something habit-forming is addictive, so it makes people feel compelled to keep using it.

clue.text: Area around which various infidels settled

indicators.note: various suggests things in assorted forms, so the letters are mixed up

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for area
taken as written before being rearranged

explanation.surface: A region where a mixed group of unbelievers made their home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settled' looks like the unbelievers putting down roots; it is the definition, as in a settled deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something finalised is settled or completed, with nothing left to agree.

clue.text: After good journey, everyone’s gobbled up food

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from bottom to top, so backwards
something gobbled is swallowed, so it ends up inside the other piece

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
a ride is a journey on a horse or in a vehicle
all means everyone

explanation.surface: After a pleasant trip, the whole party has wolfed down their meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gobbled up' reads as one phrase meaning eaten, but it holds two signals: one to swallow, one to turn the swallowed word upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: A grillade is a dish of grilled meat, so it is a kind of food.

clue.text: In place frequented by Conservative, Democrat’s put in vulnerable position

indicators.note: the Democrat is put in, placed inside the other piece

blocks.note: to hang out somewhere is to spend time in a place often
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party
D is the abbreviation for Democrat

explanation.surface: A political scandal: a Democrat at a Tory haunt finds himself exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pairs two parties, but 'hung out' comes from the place frequented, and D goes inside TORY. The 'in' does double duty, finishing the insertion and opening the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To be hung out to dry is an idiom for being left exposed and abandoned by allies, which is a vulnerable position.

clue.text: Well-behaved East End crowd on railway

indicators.note: Cockneys of London's East End famously drop their aitches, so the initial H goes

blocks.note: a horde is a large crowd
RLY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A polite London crowd queues for a train.
explanation.walkthrough: The East End is the traditional Cockney part of London, where the H of horde would not be spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: Orderly means tidy and calm, describing people who behave well and cause no disturbance.

clue.text: British football team in France getting medal

blocks.note: Br is the abbreviation for British
onze is French for eleven, the number in a football team

explanation.surface: A British football side playing in France wins a medal.
explanation.walkthrough: A football side has eleven players, and the French word for eleven is onze.
explanation.definitionFit: Bronze is the third-place medal in sporting competitions, named after the metal it is made from.

clue.text: Reacted angrily, as circular letter’s dispatched by City editor

indicators.note: something dispatched is sent away, so it is removed

blocks.note: Bristol is a city in the west of England
the round letter
ED is the abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: Someone flared up when a newspaper editor sent out a circular.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circular letter' looks like a mailshot; it is the round letter O, removed from the city's name.
explanation.definitionFit: To bristle is to show sudden anger or indignation, like an animal raising its fur.

clue.text: Individual such as Shakespeare needing no introduction as playwright

indicators.note: with no introduction the name loses its opening letter

blocks.note: one is a single individual
Shakespeare's first name, so he is an example of a Will

explanation.surface: A playwright as famous as Shakespeare needs no introduction.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'needs no introduction' sounds like praise of fame; it removes the W of WILL. The answer is spelt O'NEILL in full.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugene O'Neill was a Nobel-winning American dramatist, author of Long Day's Journey into Night.

clue.text: Not keeping time, cornet fluffed note

indicators.note: not keeping the time means losing the letter that abbreviates time
a fluffed note is played wrongly, so the letters come out in the wrong order

blocks.note: the brass instrument, taken as written before being cut

explanation.surface: A cornet player loses the beat and plays a wrong note.
explanation.walkthrough: The musical note in the surface becomes a banknote: a oncer is old British slang for a one-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: Oncer is British slang for a one-pound note, a piece of paper money.

clue.text: Artist using restored frames

indicators.note: the words frame the answer, holding it inside them like a picture

blocks.note: the letters run across the gap between these two words

explanation.surface: A painter uses frames that have been restored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frames' looks like the noun an artist uses; it is the verb that holds the answer inside two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres was a French neoclassical painter, famous for portraits and nudes.

clue.text: Transport piles of hay to sell with 25% off

indicators.note: a quarter of a four-letter word is one letter, which is cut off its end

blocks.note: ricks are stacks of hay
to hawk goods is to sell them on the street

explanation.surface: A farmer moves the haystacks to sell them at a discount.
explanation.walkthrough: The 25% off sounds like a sale price; it cuts one letter of four from the end of HAWK.
explanation.definitionFit: A rickshaw is a light two-wheeled vehicle pulled by a person, a form of transport.

clue.text: Listened to rock music

indicators.note: what is listened to is heard, not read, so a spoken form is wanted

blocks.note: a scar is a steep rocky crag

explanation.surface: Someone listened to rock music.
explanation.walkthrough: Rock music suggests one genre; the rock is a scar, which in a British accent without the R is said like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ska is a Jamaican style of popular music, a forerunner of reggae with an offbeat rhythm.

clue.text: Living in dungeon

blocks.note: first meaning: one's upkeep or livelihood
second meaning: the strongest tower of a castle, where prisoners might be held

explanation.surface: Life spent locked away in a dungeon.
explanation.definitionFit: Keep means the cost of food and lodging, and also a castle's central stronghold or donjon.

clue.text: Armed and ready to move, one has unrealistic expectations

indicators.note: the letters are made to move around into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A soldier armed and ready to march off, full of fanciful hopes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Armed and ready to move' reads as troops on alert; both words are the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A daydreamer indulges in pleasant fantasies, so tends to hope for things that are not realistic.
